A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOFFLOW-2 research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original structure prediction and MOF generation results in Tables 2–3, together with property distributions and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds GCMC evaluations of conditional generation and learned-potential energy evaluations in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Appendix G.2 adds a conditional variant whose building block generator cross-attends to the property embedding c = Linear(y) + Fourier(y). This extends the existing generator while retaining the torsion-aware structure prediction procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds property-targeted inverse design for high CO2 working capacity, extending task coverage beyond v1's structure prediction and unconditional generation. This introduces a distinct generation objective; the underlying Boyd MOF dataset remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The new conditional comparison evaluates MOFDiff using property-targeted latent optimization, whereas v1 reports its unconditional generation comparison. The existing RS, EA, DiffCSP, MOFFLOW, and ordinary MOFDiff comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Original experimental settings remain unchanged. G.2 adds GCMC evaluation, reporting 200 sampled building blocks and MOFFLOW-2 targets of 2, 3, and 4 versus MOFDiff's target of 15. G.3 evaluates 10,000 structures per model using uma-m-1.1 energy per atom.

E4.justification: G.3 adds an energy-distribution diagnostic comparing generated structures with training data and MOFDiff, supplementing the existing geometric property analyses. The metal RMSD and structure prediction property analyses are retained; no component ablation is added.

E5.justification: There is no change in repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty reporting. Neither version provides experimental confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability across training seeds.

E6.justification: Figure 9 newly reports higher achieved CO2 capacities for conditional MOFFLOW-2 under different target settings from MOFDiff, and an energy distribution closer to training data. Tables 2–3 retain their values. The main-text metal-type count changes from 7 to 7–8, matching the already reported Appendix B counts.

T1.justification: The structural definitions, flow-matching objectives, and manifold derivations in Sections 3 and 5 and Appendix C remain unchanged. No theoretical assumptions, proofs, or mathematical corrections are introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about two-stage generation, novel building blocks, torsion-aware structure prediction, and advantages over existing MOF models retain their meaning. The additional appendix experiments do not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: The earlier brief DFT-validation caveat becomes a fuller limitations section. v2 adds RDKit failure conditions for incomplete or invalid linkers, acknowledges that property conditioning affects only the building block generator, and qualifies learned-potential energy estimates relative to DFT.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a project code link in the abstract and identifies x-transformers as its sequence-model implementation in A.2. It also documents the new conditioning mechanism and UMA model version. Existing hardware and hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 removes the supplementary survey of flow matching and inorganic crystal generators, including citations to CDVAE, EquiCSP, and DiffCSP++. It adds x-transformers, RMSNorm, and UMA references. Section 2's direct MOF and equivariance positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized abstract and conclusion edits, a conference-header update, and revised cross-references. Appendix G becomes Additional experiments with subsections, while Appendix H changes from additional related work to limitations. Most narrative structure and prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel Figure 9 for working capacity and energy distributions, rewrites Figure 8's caption, and makes limited layout adjustments. Existing figures and tables largely retain their designs and content.

improvement.justification: The new GCMC and energy-distribution results add useful evidence about practical generation and physical plausibility, while code disclosure and specific limitations improve transparency. These gains are limited: conditional targets differ between methods, energy estimates remain a learned-potential proxy, and DFT validation is still absent. Removing supplementary related-work background reduces context, but the direct research positioning is retained.
